checks.question: Which LLS configuration does the testbed map to?
checks.result: LLS-C3 structure (supported); one document says LLS-C2/C3 (unresolved)
checks.finding: The v8 deck (slide 6) and the story guide (chapter 1) say the testbed has the LLS-C3 structure: grandmaster, boundary clock, radio units, no O-DU in the timing chain. The Testbed Configuration Reference (§4) says the topology 'models O-RAN LLS-C2/C3'. LLS-C2 puts the O-DU in the sync chain, which the testbed does not have. The app lights LLS-C3 as 'configured' and records the disagreement on the LLS-C2 card.

checks.question: What is the O-DU's timing role in LLS-C1/C2?
checks.finding: The project documents quote O-RAN.WG4.CUS.0 (via Armstrong) as: the O-DU is part of the synchronization chain and network timing is distributed from O-DU to O-RU. A web-search snippet (page not opened) adds that the O-DU receives network time from a PRTC/T-GM, co-located or remote. No openable source states which PTP clock type (T-BC or T-GM) the O-DU implements, so that sentence is SOURCE_NEEDED and hidden.

checks.question: What is the M-plane sync YANG model name?
checks.finding: The name 'o-ran-sync' appears in a comment in the project's own ingest/sync_status.py. Fetching the O-RAN YANG repository or specification was not possible (egress blocked / URL not found) and a web search did not return a page that confirms the module or its leaves. The sentence naming the module is SOURCE_NEEDED and hidden.

checks.question: Is the G.8271 TDD ±1.5 µs budget stated correctly?
checks.result: partly verified: ±1.5 µs at reference point E; 'TDD' framing not verified
checks.finding: The project's verification (V5_VERIFICATION_LOG item 32, V5_DISAGREEMENTS item 6) supports ±1.5 µs as an absolute time-error limit at reference point E / the end application relative to a common recognised time standard (ITU-T G.8271.1), and removes the 'O-RU to PRTC' wording. The deck separately cites a TDD cell phase synchronization of better than 3 µs (3GPP TS 38.133). No project document states how 1.5 µs and 3 µs relate or calls ±1.5 µs a 'TDD' budget, so the app does not use the word 'TDD' with 1.5 µs.

checks.question: Which WG11 S-plane threat references does the project use?
checks.result: relayed by project documents; ETSI TR 104 106 not opened
checks.finding: V8 slides 10-12 and the Parameter Fault Matrix (FAULT KEY) map: A1 to T-SPLANE-02/03 (rogue PTP instance), A5 to T-SPLANE-01 (clock service interrupted), A8 to T-SPLANE-03 (slaves given inaccurate time), C1 to T-SPLANE-04 (degradation or free-running), and T-FRHAUL-01 (compromised O-DU or link) and T-FRHAUL-02 (access paths). ETSI TR 104 106 itself could not be opened here. The title of T-SPLANE-02 is not stated in the repository.

elements.name: GM-A: primary grandmaster (PRTC/T-GM role)
elements.role: Primary time source of the testbed; wins the Best Master Clock election in normal operation.

sentences.text: In the testbed GM-A is the primary grandmaster (T-GM) with priority2 100, so it wins the Best Master Clock election in normal operation.
GM-A runs with serverOnly 1, so it serves time and never takes time from another clock.
GM-A's clockIdentity 020000fffe00000a is on the operator's allow-list; the allow-list is what lets the rule tell a planned changeover from a rogue grandmaster.
No GNSS receiver exists in the testbed: GM-A is a ptp4l process on a free-running clock that stands in for the PRTC/T-GM role, so GNSS-locked behaviour, holdover and spoofing are not measured.

elements.name: GM-B: provisioned backup grandmaster
elements.role: Allow-listed backup source that takes over in a planned or unplanned grandmaster change.

sentences.text: GM-B is the provisioned backup grandmaster with priority2 110; it enables the planned changeover scenario B2.

When GM-A fails with no maintenance window open and GM-B takes over, the frozen rule returned UNKNOWN in 12 of 12 campaign runs, because packets alone cannot tell a real failure from an attack that knocked GM-A out.
In the 5 recovery-loop runs of that case the loop took no disruptive action and escalated to an operator.

elements.name: Boundary clock (T-BC)
elements.role: Re-serves grandmaster time to the radio-unit segment; slave upstream, master downstream.

sentences.text: The boundary clock is a slave on the grandmaster segment (brUP) and a master on the radio-unit segment (brDN), with priority2 120, so radio units see stepsRemoved 1.
The recovery loop never isolates a port provisioned in the master role, because isolating the boundary clock would itself remove timing; such cases are escalated instead.

In interception scenario C1 the boundary clock's downstream port was blackholed and never restored: RU1/RU2 spent a median 39.0 s of 40 s without a master when nothing was done, and 2.5 s with the recovery loop (5 of 5 restored).

elements.name: Standby boundary clock
elements.role: Cold-standby T-BC cabled to both bridges; its daemon starts only if the loop fails over.

sentences.text: A cold-standby boundary clock with identity 020000fffe0000c5 is cabled to both bridges in every run of both arms, and its daemon starts only if the loop executes a failover.

citation.locator: 'Addition in every run of both arms'

sentences.text: The loop activates it when no Announce arrives from any provisioned master port for more than 2 s (10 s while a maintenance window is open).
Failover was executed and verified in 5 of 5 C1 runs; the same trigger fired once in a benign run (B3 replicate 17) during a real 16.5 s outage, which is why hypothesis H3 is reported as failed.

elements.name: O-RU (radio units RU1–RU3)
elements.role: Radio unit at the antenna; receives time over the Open Fronthaul S-plane.

sentences.text: In the O-RAN split the O-RU hosts Low-PHY and RF processing; radio requirements are measured at the antenna side, which in O-RAN is the O-RU.

citation.locator: functional-split figure and 'WHY THE O-RU' note

sentences.text: The testbed's three radio units are ptp4l daemons with clientOnly 1 (they only take time); the Testbed Configuration Reference labels them 'O-RU proxies (T-TSC)'.

A radio unit counts as healthy when its parent is a provisioned boundary clock, its grandmaster is on the allow-list and its port state is SLAVE or UNCALIBRATED; the evaluation scores who the radio units follow, not nanosecond time error.
130 ns is scoped by the project's verification to the relative time-alignment error for intra-band contiguous carrier aggregation, Timing Category A, not presented as a universal O-RAN limit.

elements.name: Open Fronthaul S-plane (PTP / SyncE)
elements.role: Carries time and frequency to the O-RU; the plane this project studies.

sentences.text: The Open Fronthaul carries four planes: control, user, synchronization and management; the S-plane delivers time and frequency.

citation.locator: 'Four kinds of traffic share this link'

sentences.text: The testbed runs the ITU-T G.8275.1 profile settings read back from the running system: domain 24, priority1 128, Sync 16 per second, Announce 8 per second, L2 multicast 01-1B-19-00-00-00, software timestamping.

ITU-T G.8271.1 frames ±1.5 µs as the maximum absolute time error at reference point E (the end application) relative to a common recognised time standard; the network's share at reference point C is 1100 ns.
SyncE is a physical-layer function and was not implemented in the testbed, so frequency synchronisation is not measured here.

elements.name: Attacker entry points (injector)
elements.role: Where forged or removed PTP traffic enters the testbed.

sentences.text: In the testbed an injector runs inside RU3's namespace on the radio-unit bridge for A1-style spoofing, replay, flooding, malformed frames and whole-second abuse; a rogue boundary clock bridges both segments (A8); and interception blackholes the boundary clock's downstream port (C1).

citation.locator: 'Position 1 … position 2 is A8; position 3 is C1'

sentences.text: The standards describe attackers by capability and position (internal, external, man-in-the-middle, injector), not by name.

citation.locator: RFC 7384 cl. 3.1 attacker classes, as relayed

sentences.text: Access paths named for the fronthaul are remote access widened by multi-vendor equipment, physical access to cell sites, supply-chain backdoors, and unauthorised access to the Open Fronthaul Ethernet interface.
Where the injector shares RU3's port (A2, A3, A5, C2, C3), isolating that port also stops RU3's own Delay_Req, so RU3's timing is reported separately.

elements.name: O-DU (distributed unit)
elements.role: Hosts RLC, MAC and High-PHY; the timing source for the O-RU in LLS-C1 and LLS-C2.

sentences.text: The O-DU hosts RLC, MAC and High-PHY and is joined to the O-RU by the Open Fronthaul (split 7-2x).
In LLS-C1 and LLS-C2 the O-DU is part of the synchronization chain towards the O-RU; in LLS-C3 it is not.

citation.locator: LLS table, as quoted from O-RAN.WG4.CUS.0 via Armstrong

sentences.text: The testbed has no O-DU: its timing chain is grandmaster to boundary clock to radio units, and the O-DU is not emulated.
The E2 interface ends at the O-CU-CP, O-CU-UP and O-DU and does not reach the O-RU.
In LLS-C1 and LLS-C2 the O-DU implements a specific PTP clock type (T-BC or T-GM) towards the O-RU.

citation.locator: No openable source states the O-DU's PTP clock type; the project documents say only that the O-DU is in the synchronization chain.

elements.name: Open Fronthaul M-plane (management)
elements.role: Configures and monitors the O-RU; the channel through which O-RU sync state would be read.

sentences.text: The M-plane carries configuration and monitoring of the radio unit.
The project wrote a fixture-tested parser for O-RU M-plane NETCONF/YANG synchronization telemetry; it was never run against real O-RU hardware.
The testbed has no M-plane; management queries were made with pmc, and pmc returns nothing unless it is called with -d 24.
The O-RAN M-plane YANG model that exposes O-RU synchronization state is named o-ran-sync.

citation.locator: Name appears only in a code comment (ingest/sync_status.py); not confirmed against the O-RAN WG4 M-plane specification or YANG file (egress blocked).

elements.name: SMO / Non-RT RIC
elements.role: Where a closed loop like ours maps in O-RAN; not implemented there.

sentences.text: In the project's architecture figure the Service Management and Orchestration layer with the Non-RT RIC sits above the RICs, O-CU, O-DU and O-RU.

citation.locator: 'SHOWS The full O-RAN picture (SMO, RICs, O-CU, O-DU, O-RU, core)'

sentences.text: The project's architecture survey describes the SMO and Non-RT RIC as performing non-real-time optimisation and policy generation with a typical control loop above 1 s.

A detect, decide, act and verify loop like this project's is the kind of function the survey places in that management domain; it is not implemented there, and the recovery loop here runs beside the testbed as a standalone process.

citation.locator: 'It does not change any frozen artefact'; runs beside the testbed

sentences.text: Whether such a loop would be an rApp, an SMO function or something else was not decided or evaluated, and no digital twin rehearses the action before it is taken.

elements.name: GNSS / time source (PRTC)
elements.role: Root time reference of the network; local GNSS receiver in LLS-C4.

sentences.text: In LLS-C4 the synchronization reference reaches the O-RU with no involvement of the transport network, typically from a local GNSS receiver, so the exposure is GNSS jamming or spoofing rather than PTP.
GNSS spoofing, GNSS jamming and honest GNSS holdover need a GNSS receiver and cannot be produced in the software testbed; they are shown as requiring hardware and are not measured.

citation.locator: 'Five need hardware and could not be produced'

elements.name: SyncE (frequency)
elements.role: Physical-layer frequency reference alongside PTP time.

sentences.text: ITU-T G.8262 (SyncE) is context only for this project: it is a physical-layer function.

citation.locator: 'Frequency synchronization context: ITU-T G.8262 (SyncE, not implemented here)'

sentences.text: SyncE and equipment-clock degradation (B4) need a SyncE-capable PHY and are not measured.

elements.name: Oscillator drift (B6, two-laptop measurement)
elements.role: Free-running crystal offset between two physical machines; software-only measurement.

sentences.text: Run 2 measured a relative crystal offset of +21.013 ppm (95 % interval +20.623 to +21.403 ppm) between two laptops against the same NTP reference, and the pre-registered criteria were met (ESTABLISHED).
Run 1 gave +20.161 ppm but failed a pre-registered criterion (retained samples), so it is reported as NOT ESTABLISHED.
These are consumer laptop crystals measured against NTP, not telecom-class oscillators, and the raw per-sample files are not in the repository, so only the derived figures can be shown.

elements.name: C-plane (control)
elements.role: Scheduling and beamforming commands to the O-RU; influenced if timing is lost.

sentences.text: The C-plane tells the radio unit what to do with the next slots.
What happens to C-plane traffic when S-plane timing is lost was not measured: the testbed has no O-DU or radio stack.
C-plane processing stops or is misaligned when the O-RU loses synchronization.

citation.locator: No openable source states this; demoted from tier 2 (see tier_log).

elements.name: U-plane (user)
elements.role: Radio samples, i.e. user data; influenced if timing is lost.

sentences.text: The U-plane carries the radio samples, meaning the users' data.
U-plane behaviour under timing loss was not measured in this project.
U-plane traffic stops when the O-RU loses synchronization.

citation.locator: No openable source states this; demoted from tier 2 (see tier_log).

elements.name: Air interface
elements.role: Radio link whose phase and time alignment depend on S-plane timing.

sentences.text: Cooperating radio units must transmit at the same instant for MIMO and carrier aggregation to work.

The cited 3GPP limits are cell phase synchronization better than 3 µs (TS 38.133) and time-alignment error of 65 ns for MIMO and 260 ns for intra-band contiguous carrier aggregation (TS 38.104, clause 9.6.3.2).

citation.locator: as relayed from ATIS and itecspec

elements.name: UE (user equipment)
elements.role: Phone or device served by the cell; the end of the consequence chain.

sentences.text: In one published experiment with switch PTP ports in dynamic role, the O-RU crashed about 2 s after a spoofing attack began, the 5G cell dropped and the radio needed a manual reboot; this is a measurement in that study, not a standard.
This project did not measure any service impact on user equipment.

elements.name: Near-RT RIC and xApps
elements.role: Near-real-time RAN control over E2.

sentences.text: E2 connects the RIC to the O-CU-CP, O-CU-UP and O-DU and does not reach the O-RU, so RIC KPIs over E2 do not exist at the S-plane boundary.

elements.name: O-CU (CP and UP)
elements.role: Central unit: RRC, PDCP (control) and SDAP, PDCP (user).

sentences.text: The O-CU-CP hosts RRC and PDCP for the control plane; the O-CU-UP hosts SDAP and PDCP for the user plane.

elements.name: 5G Core
elements.role: Core network reached over N2 and N3.

sentences.text: The project's architecture survey lists N2 control-plane to the AMF and N3 user-plane to the UPF as the core interfaces of the gNB.

citation.locator: 'N2 control-plane to AMF, N3 user-plane to UPF'

elements.name: O-Cloud
elements.role: Cloud infrastructure that hosts virtualised O-RAN functions, managed over O2.

sentences.text: The project's architecture survey lists O2 as the SMO interface to the O-Cloud for resource inventory, deployment and lifecycle.

elements.name: LLS-C1
elements.role: O-DU is in the sync chain; direct link to the O-RU.

sentences.text: In LLS-C1 the O-DU is part of the synchronization chain and network timing is distributed from O-DU to O-RU over a direct connection.

citation.locator: LLS-C1 row, as quoted from O-RAN.WG4.CUS.0 via Armstrong

sentences.text: A compromised O-DU or the O-DU–O-RU link controls the O-RU's time (T-FRHAUL-01).
Not the testbed's configuration: the testbed has no O-DU in its timing chain.

elements.name: LLS-C2
elements.role: O-DU is in the sync chain; one or more Ethernet switches allowed.

sentences.text: In LLS-C2 the O-DU is part of the synchronization chain and one or more Ethernet switches are allowed in the fronthaul network.

The Testbed Configuration Reference says the testbed 'models O-RAN LLS-C2/C3', while the v8 deck and story guide map it to LLS-C3 only; this app follows the latter because the testbed has no O-DU, and records the disagreement as unresolved.

elements.name: LLS-C3 (the testbed's configuration)
elements.role: O-DU not in the sync chain; PRTC/T-GM to O-RU through the network.

sentences.text: In LLS-C3 the O-DU is not part of the synchronization chain and timing is distributed from a PRTC/T-GM to the O-RU, typically from central or aggregation sites.
The testbed has the LLS-C3 structure: grandmaster to boundary clock to radio units, with no O-DU in the timing chain.
TIMESAFE's real production-style test also used LLS-C3.

elements.name: LLS-C4
elements.role: Local GNSS receiver at the O-RU; no network timing.

sentences.text: In LLS-C4 the reference is provided to the O-RU with no involvement of the transport network, typically by a local GNSS receiver.
Not the testbed's configuration, and GNSS effects are not measurable in it.

elements.name: Delay request-response exchange (t1-t4)
elements.role: How a radio unit measures its offset and the path delay.

sentences.text: The master sends Sync and then Follow_Up carrying the exact send time t1; the slave records arrival t2, sends Delay_Req at t3, and the master returns the arrival time t4 in Delay_Resp.
Assuming the same delay in both directions, mean path delay = [(t2 − t1) + (t4 − t3)] / 2 and offset from master = [(t2 − t1) − (t4 − t3)] / 2.
A real ptp4l line from baseline run 1, RU1, reads: master offset 1191 s0 freq -1547 path delay 5313, i.e. offset 1,191 ns, servo state s0 (not steering), path delay 5,313 ns.
Every ptp4l daemon runs with free_running 1, so offsets are measured but no clock is ever steered.

elements.name: Announce and the BMCA contest
elements.role: Field-by-field election of the best master from Announce messages.

sentences.text: Each clock broadcasts Announce messages and every clock runs the Best Master Clock Algorithm; fields such as priority1, clockClass, priority2 and clockIdentity are compared to elect the master.

citation.locator: 'Who is the master? The election' table

sentences.text: The G.8275.1 profile fixes priority1 at 128; the testbed uses domain 24 and the alternate BMCA (dataset_comparison G.8275.x).

In A1 replicate 1 of the campaign the rogue clock advertised clockClass 6 against the legitimate grandmaster's 248, so it won the election without breaking any field rule; only the operator's allow-list exposed it.

elements.name: Attack packets at the recorded injection point
elements.role: Where forged, flooded or removed PTP traffic entered in each recorded run.

sentences.text: For each recorded run the loop's log names the ingress port it localised the violation to (for example p-rogue in A1 and p-v-ru3 in A2, A3, A5, C2 and C3); the replay shows that port and the frame counts captured on the bridge.

Injectors for spoofing, replay, flooding, malformed frames and whole-second abuse run inside RU3's namespace; the rogue boundary clock spans both bridges; interception blackholes the boundary clock's downstream port.
Frames dropped by the isolation rule never reach the bridge capture, so after isolation the attacker's frame count falls to zero in the loop arm while it continues in the control arm.

citation.locator: 35/35 isolations present in the final nft ruleset

elements.name: Recorded per-sender packet counts
elements.role: Frames per 0.5 s per sender and message type, from each run's brDN/brUP captures.

sentences.text: Each recovery run archive contains the brDN and brUP captures (dn.pcap.gz, up.pcap.gz) next to the loop and observer logs.
Counts are attributed to senders by MAC address on the bridge, not by the switch port the frame entered on; replayed frames carry the original sender's MAC.

citation.locator: per-port roles are judged by the live loop, not by this capture

elements.name: Faults that need hardware (not measured)
elements.role: GNSS spoofing and jamming, honest holdover, SyncE degradation and oscillator drift on telecom hardware.

sentences.text: Five catalogue faults need hardware and could not be produced in software: A6 GNSS spoofing, A7 GNSS jamming, B1 holdover, B4 SyncE and B6 oscillator drift.

citation.locator: 'Five need hardware and could not be produced'

sentences.text: For B6 only a two-laptop crystal measurement exists (run 2: +21.013 ppm, ESTABLISHED); it is not a telecom-oscillator measurement.

elements.name: Recovery loop: Detect
elements.role: Loop stage 'Detect', lit from the recorded loop.jsonl events.

sentences.text: Every 1 s the frozen rule judges a 6 s sliding window of segment frames, and a second channel checks that Announce keeps arriving from a provisioned master port.

elements.name: Recovery loop: Localise
elements.role: Loop stage 'Localise', lit from the recorded loop.jsonl events.

sentences.text: Each bridge port is compared with its provisioned role: an unprovisioned port originating PTP, a client port sending master-role messages, foreign source identities or malformed frames mark a violating port.

elements.name: Recovery loop: Decide
elements.role: Loop stage 'Decide', lit from the recorded loop.jsonl events.

sentences.text: The loop acts only when at least 2 of the last 3 evaluations say ATTACK, never isolates a provisioned master-role port (it escalates instead), and fails over when no Announce arrives for more than 2 s.

elements.name: Recovery loop: Act
elements.role: Loop stage 'Act', lit from the recorded loop.jsonl events.

sentences.text: Isolation is an nftables bridge rule dropping ethertype 0x88F7 at the offending port; failover starts the cold-standby boundary clock; in the control arm the identical loop only logs would_act.

elements.name: Recovery loop: Verify
elements.role: Loop stage 'Verify', lit from the recorded loop.jsonl events.

sentences.text: Within 20 s every non-isolated radio unit must report a provisioned master-role parent, an allow-listed grandmaster and port state SLAVE or UNCALIBRATED, read with pmc -d 24.

elements.name: Recovery loop: Rollback
elements.role: Loop stage 'Rollback', lit from the recorded loop.jsonl events.

sentences.text: If verification fails the action is undone and the operator alerted.

elements.name: Recovery loop (detect → rollback)
elements.role: Closed loop beside the testbed, evaluated in 140 pre-registered runs.

sentences.text: In 140 pre-registered runs the loop restored A1 from 38.5 s to 2.0 s, C1 from 39.0 s to 2.5 s and C3 from 38.5 s to 2.0 s (median unhealthy seconds of 40).
Hypothesis H3 (no harm on benign faults) failed: one standby failover in 25 benign runs (B3 replicate 17), during a genuine 16.5 s outage.
No rollback was needed in any of the 140 runs.

elements.name: Dataset: 140 recovery-loop runs
elements.role: 14 scenarios × 2 arms × 5 replicates, loaded in the database.

sentences.text: The evaluation comprises 140 live runs: 14 scenarios, 2 arms and 5 replicates, on real linuxptp 4.0 daemons.

elements.name: Dataset: 168-run detector campaign
elements.role: 14 scenarios × 12 replicates scored by the frozen rule.

sentences.text: The detector campaign has 168 runs (14 scenarios × 12 replicates); the revised rule v3 attributed the exact fault in 84 of 96 attack runs.

elements.name: Dataset: 13 Sep pilot
elements.role: Software-testbed closed-loop pilot (S11) and its independent validation (S15).

sentences.text: In S11 a detector-triggered port failover succeeded in 5 of 5 trials against 0 of 5 no-action controls.
Independent validation S15 was not established: trigger rate above the boundary 14/15, no-trigger rate below the boundary 8/15, below the frozen 0.8.

elements.name: Data not in repo
elements.role: Raw files referenced by the project that the repository does not contain.

sentences.text: Files of 50 MB or more, including the S13 and S14 packet CSVs and the combined dataset workbooks, are kept only on the project machine.
The raw per-sample CSVs of the B6 two-laptop measurement are named with their sha256 in the analysis output but are not in the repository.
